stems: I ___ the roof, but I failed. (I attempted it)
questions.explanation: Try to do – próbować (wysiłek, często bez sukcesu); try doing – wypróbować coś, by sprawdzić, czy działa.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: I tried to fix the roof. (I attempted it, but I failed.)

stems: ___ green tea if you have a stomachache. (test it to see if it works)
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: Try drinking green tea if you have a stomachache. (Test it to see if it works.)

stems: „If you have trouble sleeping, ___ off your phone an hour before bed.” Which form gives advice to test a method?
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: If you try doing something, you test it to see if it is suitable, useful or works.

stems: ___ the dog before you leave! (Don't forget!)
questions.explanation: Remember to do – pamiętać, by coś zrobić (najpierw pamiętam, potem robię).
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: Remember to feed the dog! (Don't forget!)

stems: I ___ to school for the first time when I was five.
questions.explanation: Remember doing – mieć wspomnienie czegoś, co się zrobiło.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: I remember going to school for the first time when I was five.

stems: Oh no, I ___ the dog! It's hungry. (I didn't remember to do it)
questions.explanation: Forget to do – nie zrobić czegoś, bo się zapomniało.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: I forgot to feed the dog! (I didn't remember.)

stems: I'll never ___ the Eiffel Tower for the first time – it was amazing. (I'll always have the memory)
questions.explanation: Forget doing – (nie) pamiętać, że się coś zrobiło; I'll never forget doing = zawsze będę to pamiętać.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: If you forget doing something, you have no memory of it.

stems: I ___ my mother. (I stopped what I was doing so I could call her)
questions.explanation: Stop to do – przerwać coś, żeby zrobić coś innego (cel).
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: I stopped to call my mother. (I stopped doing something so I could call her.)

stems: I ___ TV two years ago. (I no longer watch TV)
questions.explanation: Stop doing – przestać coś robić (już tego nie robię).
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: I stopped watching TV two years ago. (I no longer watch TV.)

stems: „She stopped to smoke.” means that she:
correct: paused what she was doing in order to smoke
distractors: gave up smoking for good and never smoked again
tried smoking to see whether she liked it
remembered that she used to smoke as a teenager
forgot that she had ever smoked at all
smoked much less than she used to before
never smoked again after that day
questions.explanation: Stop to + bezokolicznik = przerwać inną czynność w celu… (tu: żeby zapalić). Stop smoking = rzucić palenie.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: If you stop to do something, you pause what you are doing in order to do something else.

stems: Choose the correct option: My idea is ___ an app.
questions.explanation: Po czasowniku be można użyć bezokolicznika z to.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: We can use a to infinitive after the verb be. My idea is to build an app.

stems: Choose the correct option: You should practise every day ___ better.
questions.explanation: Cel wyrażamy bezokolicznikiem z to (nie *for getting*).
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: You should practise every day to get better.

stems: Choose the correct option: ___ the perfect cup of tea, leave the bag in the water for three minutes.
questions.explanation: Bezokolicznik z to wyraża cel, także na początku zdania.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: To make the perfect cup of tea, leave the bag in the water for three minutes.

stems: Choose the correct option: She ran to school ___ late.
questions.explanation: So as (not) to – formalny odpowiednik to + bezokolicznik dla celu; przeczenie: so as not to.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: She ran to school so as not to be late.

stems: Choose the correct option: The house was built with big windows ___ in lots of light.
questions.explanation: So as to + bezokolicznik – formalnie wyraża cel.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: The house was built with big windows so as to let in lots of light.

stems: Choose the correct option: I passed my exams ___ hard.
questions.explanation: Po przyimku zawsze forma -ing, nie bezokolicznik.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: We use an -ing form, not a to infinitive, after a preposition. I passed my exams by working hard.

distractors: She's interested in to learn Spanish.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: We use an -ing form, not a to infinitive, after a preposition.

stems: „I tried to open the window.” suggests that:
correct: I made an effort, but it may not have worked
distractors: I opened it just to see if it would help
I remembered opening it some time before
I stopped opening it after a while
I opened it only as a kind of experiment
I forgot to open it before leaving
I opened it easily without any effort
questions.explanation: Try to do = próbować (wysiłek); try doing = sprawdzić efekt.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: If you try to do something, you make an attempt to do it.

stems: The formal alternative to a to infinitive for expressing purpose is:
questions.explanation: So as (not) to – formalny sposób wyrażenia celu.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1B: We can use so as (not) to as a formal alternative to a to infinitive, to express a purpose.
